lines.trans: It says here that Senya feeds the next clue.
Look, we continue saving on ingredients.
Here is a caviar sandwich without butter or bread.
Fedya, tell me, what should I do next?
Buy a bottle of port wine and come over this evening.
Fedya, what on earth are you talking about right now?
Vitya, why do I not see my car?
Admit it, did you already go for a ride in it?
I just reparked it in another spot.
Your car really is very good.
Well then, shall we start our new countdown?
Come back to me as soon as possible.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледующий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('next').

examples.trans: I cannot sign a new contract.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Машина у тебя действительно очень хорошая.
examples.trans: Your car really is very good.

examples.text: Машина действительно очень хорошая.
examples.trans: The car really is very good.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хочешь найти шляпку, тогда следуй подсказкам.
examples.trans: If you want to find the hat, follow the clues.

examples.text: Денис, ты ничего не хочешь мне сказать?
examples.trans: Denis, is there nothing you want to tell me?

examples.text: Витя, почему я машину свою не вижу?
examples.trans: Vitya, why do I not see my car?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Это хорошая экономия каждый месяц.
examples.trans: That is a nice savings every month.

examples.text: Витя, хорошо подумай про звезду Мишлен.
examples.trans: Vitya, think carefully about the Michelin star.

examples.text: Машина у тебя действительно очень хорошая.
examples.trans: Your car really is very good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Димочка, ну не расстраивайся ты так.
examples.trans: Dimochka, well do not get so upset.

examples.text: Ну у тебя же есть твой ресторан.
examples.trans: Well, you still have your restaurant.

examples.text: Значит, тебе нужно там что-то менять.
examples.trans: Then you need to change something there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let us begin', paired with 'начинать'.

examples.text: Нужно сначала кого-то на своё место назначить.
examples.trans: First I need to appoint someone in my place.

examples.text: Кухня, внимание, я назначаю Лаврова шефом!
examples.trans: Kitchen, attention, I am appointing Lavrov head chef!

examples.text: Для начала мы бы сели на скамейку.
examples.trans: To start with, we would have sat down on a bench.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Возвращайся, Витя, обратно в наш ресторан.
examples.trans: Come back, Vitya, back to our restaurant.

examples.text: Нагиев обещает нашему шефу звезду Мишлен.
examples.trans: Nagiyev is promising our chef a Michelin star.

examples.text: Ну что, начнём наш новый отсчёт?
examples.trans: Well then, shall we start our new countdown?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Я новый контракт не могу подписать.
examples.trans: I cannot sign a new contract.

examples.text: Баринова, что ли? Он мне даром не нужен.
examples.trans: Barinov, you mean? I do not need him even for free.

examples.text: Ну что, начнём наш новый отсчёт?
examples.trans: Well then, shall we start our new countdown?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'счёт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'countdown' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну что, начнём наш новый отсчёт?
examples.trans: Well then, shall we start our new countdown?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть отсчёт.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always countdown.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'звращаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'return', paired with 'вернуться'.

examples.text: Он всегда поздно возвращается домой.
examples.trans: He always comes home late.

examples.text: Зло всегда возвращается.
examples.trans: Evil always comes back.

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.
examples.trans: Remember: evil always comes back to the ruler.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.text: Возвращайся скорее обратно ко мне.
examples.trans: Come back to me as soon as possible.

examples.text: Так звони скорее своему другу в салон!
examples.trans: Then call your friend at the dealership right away!

examples.text: Пойдём скорее на студию!
examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Возвращайся, Витя, обратно в наш ресторан.
examples.trans: Come back, Vitya, back to our restaurant.

examples.text: Возвращайся скорее обратно ко мне.
examples.trans: Come back to me as soon as possible.

examples.text: Мне надо срочно с бумагами разобраться.
examples.trans: I urgently need to sort out some paperwork.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Димочка, ну не расстраивайся ты так.
examples.trans: Dimochka, well do not get so upset.

examples.text: Я новый контракт не могу подписать.
examples.trans: I cannot sign a new contract.

examples.text: Сейчас это уже не ресторан, а печка.
examples.trans: Right now it is no longer a restaurant, it is a furnace.
